concepts.gloss_en: The Tzaddik — the righteous leader of the generation as a mystical archetype/aspect (בחינה): head of the world, guardian of the covenant (יסוד/ברית), identified with Moshe, Yosef, Mashiach, etc.; also used collectively (צדיקים) and for the letter-symbol yud.

reason_for_human: Round-1 split הצדיק (archetype) from צדיק (generic), but reading every occurrence shows the split is spurious: the 'צדיק' bucket is dominated by definite הַצַּדִּיק in the actual text (e.g. occ:21, 324, 2528), and the indefinite צדיק is itself used for the archetype ('כל צדיק שבדור הוא בחינת משה משיח', occ:1968). The 5 'הצדיק' occurrences (the tzaddik as ראש/head from whom generations are drawn) are the same archetypal Tzaddik as the rest — no clean generic-vs-archetype boundary exists, so the article variation is inflectional here, not a homograph or archetype split. Merged into one concept.
